en: Full of quiet hints that point to other things
hook: ALLUSIVE: full of ALLUSIONS (hints), not to be confused with elusive (hard to catch).
story: Allusive. Full of quiet hints that point to other things. At a poetry evening in the city, an old poet read a verse about a red sun rising over a green field, and the boys who never came home. He never named the year. Yet the whole hall went still, because everyone knew he meant the flag and the war of independence. The poem was allusive. An allusive work is full of allusions; do not confuse it with elusive, which means hard to catch. So, what word describes writing that hints at things without naming them? ... Allusive.

gre.s: Her poems are deeply ____, packed with veiled references to Persian mystics and Bengali folk songs that most readers miss on a first reading.
gre.clue: packed with veiled references

example: The cartoonist's allusive drawings rewarded readers who knew the week's headlines, since every figure hinted at a real minister.

en: Honest and natural, with no tricks or pretense
hook: ART-LESS: no art of trickery. Natural and honest.
story: Artless. Natural and honest, without tricks or pretence. At a grand city wedding, guests were praising the decorations in polite, careful voices. Then Rick's five-year-old niece looked up at the bride and said, "Your lipstick is on your teeth." The bride [laugh] burst out laughing and fixed it. Nobody could be offended by such an artless remark. Here art means craft or cunning, as in the phrase the art of deception, so artless means free of cunning. So, what word describes words or behaviour that are innocent and natural? ... Artless.

gre.s: The child's ____ remarks, free of any calculation or flattery, charmed the guests far more than the polished speeches of the adults.
gre.clue: free of any calculation or flattery

example: Moni's artless letter to the company, written in plain words without any flattery, persuaded the director to fund her school.

en: Harsh, loud, and unpleasant-sounding
hook: CACO = bad, PHONE = sound. Bad sound.
story: Cacophonous. Harsh, loud and unpleasant to hear. At six in the evening, Tom stands at the busiest crossing in town waiting for a bus. Horns blare from every direction, a loudspeaker shouts discounts, a drill pounds the flyover, and conductors scream route names over all of it. He presses his hands to his ears. The noise is cacophonous. Think of a symphony, sounds in harmony; cacophonous is the opposite, from Greek words meaning bad sound. So, what word describes a harsh, jarring mix of noises? ... Cacophonous.

gre.s: The composer deliberately made the opening ____, layering clashing rhythms and harsh brass so that the gentle melody that follows seems all the sweeter.
gre.clue: layering clashing rhythms and harsh brass

example: Rush hour at Farmgate is cacophonous, a blare of bus horns, shouting conductors and revving motorbike engines.

en: A lie told on purpose to ruin someone's good name
hook: CALUMNY sounds like 'CALL YOU MONEY-thief', a lie that ruins your name.
story: Calumny. A false statement made on purpose to damage someone's good name. When Rachel became the first woman to chair the school committee in her district, anonymous posts appeared claiming she had stolen from the school fund. None of it was true; the accounts showed every cent. Yet neighbours whispered as she passed. The calumny hurt her more than any honest criticism could. Calumny comes from a Latin word for a false accusation. So, what noun means a deliberate lie that ruins a person's good name? ... Calumny.

gre.s: The memoir was less a balanced history than an act of ____, attributing invented crimes to the author's former rivals.
gre.clue: attributing invented crimes

example: Anonymous accounts spread calumny about the young journalist, claiming she had been paid by foreign spies.

en: Resting on guesses rather than solid proof
hook: CONJECTURE = a guess. CONJECTURAL = guess-based.
story: Conjectural. Based on guesswork rather than solid proof. At an ancient ruined city in the north, a guide told Andy's group that a certain grassy mound was once a royal palace. When Andy asked how he knew, the guide admitted that nobody had ever dug there. The palace was purely conjectural. Andy liked the story anyway. A conjecture is a guess, from a Latin verb meaning to throw together, so a conjectural claim throws a few facts together into a guess. So, what word describes a claim built on guesses, not proof? ... Conjectural.

gre.s: Because no fossils from the period have been found, any account of the species' behavior must remain largely ____.
gre.clue: no fossils from the period have been found

example: Since the ancient city left no written records, our picture of its government is mostly conjectural.

en: To move or act slowly and waste time
hook: DAWDLE: like a DOODLE, wasting time drawing nothing.
story: Dawdle. To move slowly and waste time. Every morning, Mandy's little brother takes forty minutes to walk to a school five minutes away. He stops to watch a goat, kicks a stone along the lane, counts the rickshaws, and buys a single tamarind sweet. Their mother stands at the gate calling, "Stop dawdling!" [sigh] He waves and dawdles on. Hear doodle in dawdle: doodling and dawdling both waste time on nothing in particular. So, what verb means to linger and waste time? ... Dawdle.

gre.s: With the deadline only hours away, the team could not afford to ____; every minute spent idling would make the final report weaker.
gre.clue: every minute spent idling

example: The children dawdled on the way home from school, stopping at every stall that sold pickles and ice lollies.

en: Rigidly applying a theory without regard for practical considerations
hook: DOCTRINAIRE: follows the DOCTRINE no matter what.
story: Doctrinaire. Rigidly sticking to a theory, whatever the real situation. A new officer sent a rule to the wetland village schools: every class must start at exactly nine. But in the monsoon, half the children came by boat across a flooded wetland, and nine o'clock meant crossing in the morning storms. Teachers begged; the officer refused. "Rules are rules." His doctrinaire attitude helped nobody. Doctrinaire comes from doctrine, a fixed set of teachings: a doctrinaire person follows the doctrine even when it fails. So, what word describes someone who applies a theory rigidly, ignoring real life? ... Doctrinaire.

gre.s: Unlike her ____ predecessor, who insisted on following party ideology even when it produced obvious failures, the new minister was willing to adapt policies to local conditions.
gre.clue: insisted on following party ideology even when it produced obvious failures

example: The doctrinaire economist insisted that markets would fix everything, even as prices of rice and lentils doubled.

en: To teach someone in a way that improves their mind or character
hook: EDIFY: builds you up like an EDIFICE (building).
story: Edify. To teach someone in a way that improves their mind or character. Every Friday afternoon, Abby's grandfather gathered the children of the lane on his veranda. He told stories of honest farmers and brave boatmen, each ending with a question to think about. Years later, Abby realised those evenings had edified her more than any textbook. Edify shares its root with edifice, a building: to edify someone is to build up their mind and character. So, what verb means to instruct in a way that improves a person morally or intellectually? ... Edify.

gre.s: The museum's new exhibits are designed to ____ as well as entertain, teaching visitors about climate science through interactive games.
gre.clue: teaching visitors about climate science

example: Her grandfather's long evening stories were meant to edify as much as amuse, each one ending with a lesson about honesty.

en: Shameless boldness; insolent nerve
hook: EFFRONTERY: right in your FRONT, shamelessly.
story: Effrontery. Shameless, insolent boldness. At the passport office, Lucy had waited in line for three hours under a hot tin roof. Then a man in sunglasses walked straight to the front, pushed his form through the window, and complained loudly that the clerk was too slow. The whole line [gasp] went silent at his effrontery. The clerk calmly handed the form back. Effrontery grows from the Latin frons, meaning forehead, as in front: effrontery is barefaced cheek, shown right to your face. So, what noun means shameless, insolent nerve? ... Effrontery.

gre.s: Caught plagiarizing an entire chapter, the author had the ____ to accuse his critics of jealousy, as though they rather than he were at fault.
gre.clue: as though they rather than he were at fault

example: The contractor who built the crumbling bridge had the effrontery to bid for the job of repairing it.

en: Possible to account for with a reason
hook: EXPLICABLE: can be EXPLAINED.
story: Explicable. Able to be explained; having a clear reason. Every night at exactly midnight, Nina's dorm room filled with a strange tapping sound. Her roommates were sure it was a ghost. [chuckle] Nina climbed onto a chair with a torch and found the cause: a loose pipe that knocked whenever the water tank on the roof refilled. The mystery was perfectly explicable after all. Most people know inexplicable, meaning impossible to explain; take away the in, and explicable means it can be explained. So, what word describes something that has a clear, logical explanation? ... Explicable.

gre.s: What at first seemed a baffling drop in sales became perfectly ____ once analysts noticed that a rival had launched a cheaper product that month.
gre.clue: once analysts noticed

example: The strange lights over the village became explicable once someone found the drone hobbyist living by the river.

en: Very fertile; capable of producing abundantly; intellectually productive
hook: FECUND: FERTILE and fruitful; produces a FECUND harvest.
story: Fecund. Very fertile; producing richly; also, full of new ideas. Each year, floods leave a fresh layer of silt on the fields along the great river. When the water goes down, Sam's father scatters seed, and within weeks the land bursts green with rice, mustard and lentils. "This soil is fecund," he says proudly. Sam sees the same thing in his young cousin, a writer with a fecund imagination who fills a notebook every week. Fecund comes from the Latin fecundus, meaning fruitful. So, what word describes soil, or a mind, that produces abundantly? ... Fecund.

gre.s: The novelist's ____ imagination produced more than forty books in two decades, each populated by dozens of memorable characters.
gre.clue: produced more than forty books in two decades

example: The delta's fecund silt allows farmers in Bangladesh to grow three crops of rice on the same field each year.

en: To refrain from doing something; to hold back
hook: FOR-BEAR: BEAR (endure) it FOR now, and hold yourself back.
story: Forbear. To hold yourself back from doing something. At a family dinner, Tara's uncle mocked her choice to study history. "What job will that get you?" Tara felt a hot reply rise to her tongue. She looked at her grandmother at the head of the table, took a slow breath, [sigh] and forbore. Later, alone with her uncle, she explained her plans calmly. Do not confuse forbear with forebear, an ancestor; to forbear is to bear your feelings and hold back. So, what verb means to refrain from doing something you want to do? ... Forbear.

gre.s: Though provoked repeatedly by the hecklers, the speaker managed to ____ from responding and simply continued his talk.
gre.clue: simply continued his talk

example: Doctors urged my diabetic grandfather to forbear eating sweets, yet every Eid he quietly helped himself to a bowl of shemai.

en: A messy, tangled situation that is hard to escape
hook: IMBROGLIO: an EMBROIDERY of tangled threads.
story: Imbroglio. A confused, tangled situation that is hard to get out of. It started when Isabel's aunt booked a community hall for her daughter's wedding, on the very date another family had booked it for their son's. Both families had receipts. The manager blamed the owner, the owner blamed a clerk, and soon three cousins, two lawyers and a local councillor were shouting in the hall. It was a full imbroglio. Imbroglio comes from an Italian word meaning to tangle, the same idea as being embroiled. So, what noun means a confusing, tangled mess? ... Imbroglio.

gre.s: What began as a minor accounting error grew into a diplomatic ____ involving three governments, two banks, and a tangle of contradictory lawsuits.
gre.clue: a tangle of contradictory lawsuits

example: A double-booked wedding hall in Uttara led to an imbroglio involving two families, three caterers and the local police.

en: Free from injury or violation; untouched
hook: IN-VIOLATE: NOT VIOLATED.
story: Inviolate. Untouched, unharmed, never broken or violated. Near a village in the hills, a small patch of forest stands around an old shrine. For generations, nobody has cut a single tree there, not even in hard winters when firewood was scarce. Monkeys swing through the branches, and the air smells of wet leaves. To the villagers the forest is inviolate, and they mean to keep it inviolate for their grandchildren. In means not, so inviolate simply means not violated. So, what word describes something kept pure and untouched? ... Inviolate.

gre.s: For centuries the sacred grove remained ____: villagers believed that anyone who cut even a single branch would bring disaster on the whole community.
gre.clue: anyone who cut even a single branch would bring disaster

example: The scholar kept her promise of confidentiality inviolate, refusing to name her sources even when a court demanded it.

en: Completely clear and transparent; easy to understand
hook: LIMPID: clear as a LIMPID pool where you can see the bottom.
story: Limpid. Perfectly clear and transparent; also, easy to understand. In the northeastern hills, Aaron waded into a stream flowing down from the hills, so clear that he could count the pebbles around his feet and watch tiny fish dart between them. [gasp] He had never seen water like it. Later, reading a favourite essay on the bus home, he noticed the prose had the same limpid quality. Limpid is the opposite of turbid: turbid water is muddy, limpid water lets you see to the bottom. So, what word describes water, or writing, that is perfectly clear? ... Limpid.

gre.s: Unlike his convoluted early essays, the philosopher's later works are written in ____ prose that even beginners can follow.
gre.clue: that even beginners can follow

example: Divers in the limpid waters around Saint Martin's Island can watch coral and fish several meters below the surface.

en: Looking or sounding sad and dismal
hook: LUGUBRIOUS: LUG-ubrious, LUGGING sadness around.
story: Lugubrious. Looking or sounding sad and gloomy, often more than the moment needs. Whenever the national team loses a cricket match, Frank's uncle plays mournful old songs on the radio, sits on the veranda with a long face, and sighs at every passing bird. His voice drops to a whisper, as if the world has ended. His wife [chuckle] just brings him tea and waits. Within a day, his lugubrious mood passes. Lugubrious comes from a Latin verb meaning to mourn: a lugubrious face looks as if it is in mourning. So, what word describes a gloomy, mournful manner? ... Lugubrious.

gre.s: The director's films are relentlessly ____: long, slow scenes of grieving widows set to funeral music leave audiences longing for even a moment of levity.
gre.clue: long, slow scenes of grieving widows set to funeral music

example: The lugubrious face of the bloodhound made the children feel sorry for it, though it was perfectly content.

en: Sentimental in an exaggerated or false way
hook: MAWKISH: makes you want to say 'mock-ish', sickly sweet.
story: Mawkish. Sentimental in an exaggerated, sickly sweet way. The holiday television drama ended with a scene that lasted ten minutes. Rain poured, violins swelled, the hero knelt in the mud, and his mother's tears fell in slow motion while a sad song played twice. Sadie's grandmother wept, but Sadie [laugh] groaned and reached for the remote. It was far too mawkish for her. Mawkish once meant sickly or nauseated: mawkish sentiment is so sugary it makes you a little sick. So, what word describes feeling laid on so thick that it seems false? ... Mawkish.

gre.s: The critic praised the film for treating its tragic subject with restraint, avoiding the ____ excesses of earlier versions that had wallowed in tearful melodrama.
gre.clue: wallowed in tearful melodrama

example: The wedding video was spoiled by mawkish background music that swelled whenever anyone so much as smiled.

en: To calm someone's anger or anxiety
hook: MOLLIFY: make MOLLY soft and calm again.
story: Mollify. To calm someone's anger or worry; to soften them. Rosie forgot her best friend Tina's birthday, and Tina stopped answering her calls. So Rosie cooked Tina's favourite chicken roast, wrote a long handwritten note, and turned up at her door on Friday afternoon. Tina tried to stay cold, [chuckle] but the smell won. By evening she was fully mollified. Mollify comes from the Latin mollis, meaning soft: to mollify someone is to soften their anger. So, what verb means to calm someone who is angry or upset? ... Mollify.

gre.s: Hoping to ____ the furious passengers, the airline manager promised full refunds and apologized personally to each traveller.
gre.clue: promised full refunds and apologized personally

example: The landlord mollified the angry tenants by lowering the rent for the months their water supply had failed.

en: Having a strong spiritual or mysterious quality
hook: NUMINOUS: sounds like LUMINOUS, glowing with something divine.
story: Numinous. Having a strong spiritual or mysterious quality; filled with a sense of the sacred. Before dawn at a Buddhist monastery in the hills, Isaac sat at the back of the prayer hall. Candles flickered before a golden statue, and monks chanted in low voices. He was not a Buddhist, yet he felt a deep stillness, as if something vast were present. The moment was numinous. Numinous comes from the Latin numen, a divine presence; do not confuse it with luminous, which only means glowing. So, what word describes an experience full of the sacred and mysterious? ... Numinous.

gre.s: Visitors describe the ancient forest as almost ____, a place whose silence and towering trees seem to suggest a divine presence.
gre.clue: seem to suggest a divine presence

example: Standing alone in the vast cathedral at dawn, the tourist felt a numinous hush that she could not explain.

en: Stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or action
hook: OB-DURATE: DURABLE stubbornness, hardened.
story: Obdurate. Stubbornly refusing to change your mind. Year after year, the parents in Jenna's village asked the owner of the school building to fix its cracked roof before the rains. He listened, nodded, and did nothing. Even when water dripped onto the children's exam papers, he refused to spend a single cent. The headmistress, the union chairman and finally a journalist all pleaded. He stayed obdurate. Obdurate shares its root with durable, from the Latin for hard: an obdurate person has hardened like stone. So, what word describes someone who stubbornly refuses to change? ... Obdurate.

gre.s: Despite mounting evidence that his policy was failing, the minister remained ____, refusing even to consider the modest changes his own advisors proposed.
gre.clue: refusing even to consider the modest changes

example: My obdurate aunt would not leave her flooded house in Sirajganj until the water reached her kitchen shelves.

en: Deceitfulness; betrayal of trust
hook: PERFIDY: per-FID-y, breaking FIDelity (faithfulness).
story: Perfidy. Deceitful betrayal of trust. In seventeen fifty-seven, at the Battle of Plassey, the young ruler of Bengal trusted his commander. But the commander had secretly made a deal with the British, and he held his troops back while the battle was lost. To this day, his name is a byword for perfidy across the region. Perfidy comes from the Latin for breaking faith, and it is related to fidelity: perfidy destroys fidelity. So, what noun means treacherous betrayal of trust? ... Perfidy.

gre.s: The spy's ____ came to light only after his death, when documents revealed that he had sold his country's secrets for decades.
gre.clue: sold his country's secrets for decades

example: Bengali schoolbooks still recall the perfidy of Mir Jafar, whose betrayal at Plassey helped the British win the battle.

en: Self-important, overly formal behavior or speech
hook: POMPOSITY: POMP and show of importance.
story: Pomposity. Self-important, overly grand behaviour or speech. At the opening of a small town library, a visiting official took the microphone for what was meant to be five minutes. He spoke for an hour, listing his own achievements in words so long that the children in the front row began to giggle. The library itself, he forgot to mention. The audience wilted under all that pomposity. Pomposity comes from pomp, a grand show of splendour: a pompous speaker puts on a show of his own importance. So, what noun means a puffed-up air of self-importance? ... Pomposity.

gre.s: The ambassador's ____ was legendary: he insisted on being addressed by all three of his honorary titles and once refused to enter a hall through a side door.
gre.clue: insisted on being addressed by all three of his honorary titles

example: The new principal's pomposity amused the students, who mimicked his habit of quoting Latin at morning assembly.

en: One of the many results, often hidden, that follow a decision
hook: RAMIFICATION: branches (rami) spreading out from a decision.
story: Ramification. One of the many results, often unexpected, that follow a decision. When a big garment factory moved its night shift two hours later, it seemed a small change. Then the tea stalls outside lost their evening customers, the local buses changed their timetable, and mothers working there needed someone new to collect their children from school. Every decision has ramifications. Ramification comes from the Latin ramus, a branch: a single choice branches out in many directions. So, what noun means one of the many branching consequences of a decision? ... Ramification.

gre.s: The committee hastily approved the plan without weighing a single ____ of its decision; within a year, unforeseen effects had rippled through every department.
gre.clue: unforeseen effects had rippled through every department

example: Few voters grasped the ramifications of the trade deal until local jute mills began closing one after another.

en: Calm and showing little emotion; dull
hook: STOLID: SOLID as a stone, no emotion shows.
story: Stolid. Calm and showing little emotion, sometimes to the point of dullness. At his son's graduation, every parent was clapping and waving phones. Earl sat with his hands on his knees, his face as still as a wall. His son worried he was disappointed. But that night, Earl quietly framed the certificate and hung it in his shop for every customer to see. His stolid face had hidden a full heart. Hear solid inside stolid: a stolid face is as solid and unmoving as stone. So, what word describes someone who shows little emotion? ... Stolid.

gre.s: Even when the verdict was announced and his family erupted in tears, the defendant remained ____, his face betraying no hint of relief or anguish.
gre.clue: his face betraying no hint of relief or anguish

example: The stolid ferry captain steered through the storm without a word while passengers clung to the railings in panic.

en: To include or absorb something into a larger category
hook: SUB-SUME: SUM it UNDER a larger heading.
story: Subsume. To include something within a larger group or category. When Nadia started a small online bakery from her kitchen, she made separate pages for cakes, cookies, brownies and pastries. Customers got lost clicking between them. Her brother suggested one simple heading: sweet treats. Now every item is subsumed under that single category, and her orders have doubled. [laugh] Sub means under, and sumere means to take: to subsume is to take something under a bigger heading. So, what verb means to fold something into a larger category? ... Subsume.

gre.s: Some linguists think it misleading to ____ Chittagonian into the broader category of Bengali dialects, since speakers of the two can barely understand each other.
gre.clue: since speakers of the two can barely understand each other

example: After the merger, the small regional bank was subsumed under its partner's brand, and its old logo disappeared from every branch.

en: Promoting a particular point of view, especially a controversial one; biased
hook: TENDENTIOUS: has a TENDENCY to favor one side.
story: Tendentious. Pushing one particular point of view, especially a disputed one; biased. A video about a proposed bridge went viral in a small town. It showed only smiling supporters, played triumphant music over every scene, and cut away whenever a farmer began to explain how his land would be lost. Abigail's journalism teacher played it in class and asked what was missing. "The other side," said Abigail. It was a tendentious film. Tendentious comes from tendency: a tendentious report tends toward one side. So, what word describes reporting that is slanted to favour one view? ... Tendentious.

gre.s: The reviewer dismissed the study as ____, noting that its authors had selected only the evidence that supported their political agenda.
gre.clue: selected only the evidence that supported their political agenda

example: The textbook's tendentious account of the war praised one general endlessly and ignored the civilians who suffered.

en: Eager to argue or fight; aggressively defiant
hook: TRUCULENT: like a TRUCK driver ready to fight anyone in traffic.
story: Truculent. Aggressive and defiant, eager to fight. When a traffic sergeant at the busy crossing stopped a speeding minibus, the driver leapt out shouting. He jabbed his finger at the sergeant's chest, refused to show his licence, and dared the officer to fine him. Passengers shrank back in their seats. The sergeant stayed calm, and the driver's truculent behaviour cost him his licence. Truculent comes from the Latin trux, meaning fierce or savage: a truculent person is fierce and ready for a fight. So, what word describes someone aggressively defiant and quick to fight? ... Truculent.

gre.s: The ____ witness refused to answer even routine questions, glaring at the prosecutor and threatening to walk out of the courtroom.
gre.clue: glaring at the prosecutor and threatening to walk out

example: Grounded for a week, the truculent teenager slammed doors and refused to speak to anyone at dinner.

en: Complete and unreserved; pure
hook: UN-ALLOYED: pure gold, not mixed into an ALLOY.
story: Unalloyed. Complete and pure, with nothing mixed in. When the national under-nineteen team won the cricket World Cup, Jim was watching on a tiny phone at a village tea stall. The moment the winning run was hit, the whole crowd [gasp] leapt up, strangers hugging strangers, [laugh] cups of tea flying. There was no worry, no doubt, nothing but joy. It was unalloyed happiness. An alloy is a mix of metals, like brass, so unalloyed joy is pure, like gold with nothing mixed in. So, what word describes a feeling that is pure and complete? ... Unalloyed.

gre.s: Her joy at the verdict was hardly ____, for though her brother had been freed, the real culprit had escaped justice entirely.
gre.clue: though her brother had been freed, the real culprit had escaped justice

example: For the village, the news that its girls' team had reached the national final brought unalloyed delight.

en: A feeling of irritation or worry caused by something troubling
hook: VEXATION: VEXED, constantly bothered.
story: Vexation. Irritation or worry caused by something troubling. Tamara spent three hours filling in an online university application, scanning every certificate and typing every address. On the final page she pressed submit, and the screen went white. Session expired. Everything was gone. She stared at the screen, [sigh] then shut the laptop and walked out to the balcony to calm her vexation. Vexation comes from vex, from a Latin verb meaning to shake or harass, and a vexing problem does shake your nerves. So, what noun means a feeling of annoyance or frustration? ... Vexation.

gre.s: Much to the ____ of the organizers, heavy rain forced them to cancel the outdoor concert just an hour before it was due to begin.
gre.clue: forced them to cancel the outdoor concert

example: To the vexation of the commuters, the metro rail stopped between stations for forty minutes without any announcement.

en: Speaking fluently, readily, and continuously
hook: VOLUBLE: speaks in VOLUMES.
story: Voluble. Speaking easily, quickly and at length. Neal's grandmother is the heart of every family wedding. She greets each guest by name, tells the story of how she met her husband, explains three recipes, gives advice on marriage, and never seems to pause for breath. Children gather around her, laughing at her jokes. Everyone agrees she is wonderfully voluble. Voluble comes from a Latin verb meaning to roll: from a voluble speaker, words simply roll out. So, what word describes someone who talks fluently and without stopping? ... Voluble.

gre.s: Usually ____ at dinner parties, chatting easily with strangers for hours, the novelist became oddly taciturn whenever anyone asked about her new book.
gre.clue: chatting easily with strangers for hours

example: The voluble street vendor kept up a steady stream of jokes and sales talk, never pausing to catch his breath.
